body.summary: Gideon Nav, an indentured servant on the bone-and-tomb world of the Ninth House, tries to escape her dreary life and her nemesis Harrowhark Nonagesimus, the Reverend Daughter. Harrow forces her into service as cavalier primary, and the two travel to Canaan House on the First House, where the heirs of the nine Houses compete to become Lyctors. They solve locked-room necromantic trials, uncover murders, and discover that the dying Seventh House adept Dulcinea is really Cytherea the First, an ancient Lyctor bent on luring the Emperor back to kill him. ||Gideon sacrifices herself on iron spikes so Harrow can absorb her soul and become a Lyctor; Harrow kills Cytherea and wakes aboard the Emperor's ship, where he names her Harrowhark the First.||

arcs.summary: Gideon's repeated escape attempts end when Harrow forces her into the cavalier role and takes her off-world.
The heirs gather at Canaan House and learn the only rule: never open a locked door without permission.
Harrow and Gideon complete the construct trial and win a key, learning to share perception.
Magnus and Abigail are found dead, then Isaac and Jeannemary are killed, driving the Houses to turn on one another.
Harrow reveals the Ninth's secret: two hundred children died so she could be born, and Gideon survived the gas.
Ianthe becomes a Lyctor by eating Naberius; Silas and Colum die fighting her.
Palamedes confronts Cytherea and destroys himself to wound her; Gideon sacrifices herself so Harrow can ascend.

themes: sacrifice and the cost of power
grief and the dead who linger
necromancy as control over life and death

notable_scenes.summary: Harrow duels Gideon on the landing field with skeletons hidden in the dirt and wins her service.
Harrow reveals her dead parents as puppets at the muster and reads the Emperor's summons.
Gideon fights Naberius in the training room and punches him after being disarmed.
Gideon and Harrow fight the regenerating construct in the Response chamber, guided by shared sight.
The Fifth House couple are found dead at the foot of the facility ladder.
Harrow tells Gideon the truth of the two hundred dead children in the pool.
Gideon throws herself onto the iron spikes so Harrow can absorb her and become a Lyctor.
